version.changelog: v1.6.0: Persist trusted peers to disk - trust survives gateway restarts and reboots

llm.summary: The package appears to implement local UDP agent-to-agent messaging as described; its network relay and webhook wake-up features are powerful but documented and optional.

dimensions.detail: The code, README and SKILL.md implement LAN discovery, send/receive, peer trust, persistence and an optional relay and webhook wake-up — all directly relevant to a 'local UDP messenger'. There are no unrelated cloud credentials or surprising binaries requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions and code remain within the messaging/trust domain, but the skill can forward copies of every message to a configured relay server and can POST to the local Gateway /hooks/agent to trigger agent turns when a hook token is configured. Those behaviors are described in the docs, but they materially change what happens at runtime (possible outbound network traffic or automatic agent wake-ups) and should be consciously enabled by the user.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The registry entry is instruction-first (no aggressive installer). The SKILL.md suggests installing via the OpenClaw plugin system (npm/GitHub), and the bundled files include the TypeScript plugin code. No arbitrary third-party download URLs or extract-from-unknown-host installs are present in the package itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables but the code and docs optionally read a gateway hook token (OPENCLAW_HOOK_TOKEN) and openclaw.json entries. That token enables active wake-ups (POSTs to localhost /hooks/agent). Also the optional relayServer, if configured to a host outside your LAN, will forward copies of all messages off-host. These are legitimate features but involve sensitive tokens and potential data exfiltration paths and should be considered before enabling.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The plugin persists trusted peers to a file in the user's home (~/.openclaw/extensions/openclaw-udp-messenger/trusted-peers.json) and keeps an in-memory message log. It does not request 'always' privileges or modify other plugins' configs, but it can trigger agent turns autonomously if a hook token is available — combine that with relay settings to understand the broader blast radius.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it claims (local UDP discovery and messaging). Before installing: 1) Decide whether you want automatic 'agent wake-up' — that requires a Gateway hook token (can be set in openclaw.json or OPENCLAW_HOOK_TOKEN) and lets the plugin POST to 127.0.0.1:/hooks/agent to start agent turns. 2) Only configure relayServer if you trust the destination — enabling it forwards copies of every message to that server (possible data exfiltration). 3) Trusted peers are saved to ~/.openclaw/extensions/openclaw-udp-messenger/trusted-peers.json; review and manage that file if needed. 4) Use 'always-confirm' mode and conservative max_exchanges on untrusted networks. 5) If you require stronger assurance, review the included index.ts source yourself (or run it in a sandboxed environment) before enabling wake-up or relay features.
